_comment: Every colour the asset map draws in. Single source of truth: AssetMap.astro imports this and scripts/test-contrast.mjs checks each entry against the sampled ocean colours of every basemap in basemap-ocean.json. Add a colour here, not in the component.
_currents: Warm pale amber, slow to fast. Amber rather than blue because the two bathymetries are opposite in tone — Esri Ocean is light, GEBCO dark — and no blue clears both: any blue pale enough to show on GEBCO's navy lands inside Esri's ocean, and GEBCO's own water runs blue through cyan to the pale mint it paints shallow banks. Amber sits outside that whole range, so one ramp serves both maps and there is no basemap switching to get wrong. Kept pale rather than saturated so the particles are not mistaken for the orange USV markers.
_sst: The temperature ramp, cold to warm: deep magenta through violet and blue to cyan and spring green. Chosen by search rather than by eye — scripts/lib/colour.mjs scores a candidate on how far it travels perceptually end to end, and the winner is the most travelled ramp that still clears every marker and particle colour by CIEDE2000 22. This one covers ΔE 122 against 44 for the muted band it replaced, at a worst clearance of 22.8. It stays out of the warm half of the wheel for the reason the gate enforces: this layer becomes the water under everything else, and red, orange and yellow are already spoken for by storms, USVs and Argo — a conventional blue-to-red ramp put orange USVs ΔE 9.3 from their own background, in the tropics, which is where the storms are. Cold is magenta rather than dark because the charcoal measuring line lives at the bottom of the lightness range, and the warm end stops short of pale because the current particles are near-white. Read the numbers from the legend, which is per view, not from a red-means-hot instinct.
_separation: Argo dots are gold, which sits about ΔE 18 from the current particles — under the bar the gate applies elsewhere. No yellow clears them: the particles are pale amber because that is the one hue reading on both bathymetries, and paling the ramp far enough to make room drops its own water contrast to 79%. The dots are therefore given a dark outline, which separates a discrete dot from a drifting trail whatever the fill does. Recorded as a named exemption rather than by lowering the threshold, so the compromise stays visible.
_measure: The measuring line. Dark rather than bright because it is drawn over everything and must not be mistaken for a platform or a current; charcoal was the only candidate clearing both bathymetries while staying clear of every feature colour. It carries a light halo, which like the track casings is an outline rather than a feature colour and so is themed in CSS rather than gated here.
